/about/: About Home About Kestrel Ridge College is an independent, co-educational school for students from Kindergarten to Year 12. The College sits on twenty hectares of bushland on the edge of the Kestrel Ridge escarpment. Around 1,100 students learn across two schools: the Junior School (Kindergarten to Year 6) and the Senior School (Years 7 to 12). We are a not-for-profit school governed by the Kestrel Ridge Education Society, a board of parents, former students and community members. At a glance Junior School Senior School Year levels Kindergarten to Year 6 Years 7 to 12 Students Around 420 Around 680 Average class size 22 24 (Years 7-10), 16 (Years 11-12) School day 8:40 am to 3:10 pm 8:30 am to 3:20 pm The eucalypt walk links the Junior and Senior Schools. /about/principals-welcome/: Principal's Welcome Home About Principal's Welcome A letter from our Principal, Dr Miriam Okonkwo-Hale. Dear families, Thank you for your interest in Kestrel Ridge College. Choosing a school is one of the most important decisions a family makes, and I hope these pages give you a real sense of who we are. Our students are curious. They ask good questions and they are not afraid to get things wrong on the way to getting them right. Our teachers are experts in their subjects, but more than that, they are experts in young people. They notice when a student is ready for a challenge, and they notice when a student needs a quiet word of encouragement. We are also a school that looks outward. Our students plant trees along Ridgeway Creek, volunteer at the community pantry, perform for local aged-care residents and compete against schools across the state. The best way to understand Kestrel Ridge is to visit. I would be delighted to welcome you at one of our Open Mornings, or you can make an enquiry and our Registrar will arrange a personal tour. Warm regards, Dr Miriam Okonkwo-Hale Principal About Principal's Welcome Our History Vision & Values
/about/our-history/: Our History Home About Our History From a single weatherboard classroom in 1962 to a Kindergarten to Year 12 school of 1,100 students. Kestrel Ridge College was founded in 1962 by a group of local families who wanted a co-educational school close to home. The first 38 students met in a weatherboard hall on Ridgeway Drive, taught by two teachers and a part-time music master. 1962 to 1979: Early years The Ridgeway Building, with its clock tower, opened in 1966. By 1975 the College had grown to 400 students and its first Year 12 class sat the Higher School Certificate. 1980 to 1999: A Kindergarten to Year 12 school The Junior School opened in 1988, making Kestrel Ridge a Kindergarten to Year 12 school. The Great Hall followed in 1994, built largely with funds raised by the Parents and Friends Association. 2000 to today The Performing Arts Centre opened in 2003 and the Science Centre in 2011. In 2019 the Fairweather Library was renovated as a light-filled learning commons, named for the College's first librarian. The Ridgeway Building has been the heart of the College since 1966. /about/vision-and-values/: Vision & Values Home About Vision & Values Our vision is for every student to become a curious, kind and capable young adult. Four values guide everything we do, from the classroom to the sports field. Curiosity We ask questions, look for evidence and enjoy learning for its own sake. Kindness We treat others with respect, include people and look after one another. Courage We try new things, speak up for what is right and learn from our mistakes. Community We belong to something bigger than ourselves, and we give back to it. Be curious, be kind, be brave, belong. — The College motto About Principal's Welcome Our History Vision & Values

Tuition fees All amounts are fictional and include GST where it applies. Fees can be paid each term, each month or once a year. Year level Annual tuition Per term Building levy Kindergarten to Year 2 $11,480 $2,870 $600 Year 3 to Year 6 $13,960 $3,490 $600 Year 7 to Year 10 $19,720 $4,930 $900 Year 11 to Year 12 $22,160 $5,540 $900 Other costs An application fee of $150 is payable with each application, and an enrolment deposit of $1,500 secures a place. /learning/: Learning Home Learning A broad, challenging curriculum from Kindergarten to the Higher School Certificate. Learning at Kestrel Ridge follows the NSW curriculum, taught by specialist teachers who bring their subjects to life. Students build strong foundations in literacy and numeracy, then go deeper with every year. Explore the Junior School , the Senior School , our co-curricular program and how we look after student wellbeing . In this section Junior School Senior School Co-curricular Wellbeing
/learning/junior-school/: Junior School Home Learning Junior School Kindergarten to Year 6: a joyful, secure start to school. The Junior School has its own buildings, playgrounds and library, and around 420 students. Each class has a home teacher, supported by specialists in music, visual arts, physical education, languages and library. What students learn English and Mathematics every day, with small-group support and extension. Science and Technology , including coding from Year 3. History and Geography , with local studies of the ridge and the creek. French from Kindergarten. Creative Arts : music, drama, dance and visual arts. Outdoor learning Every class spends at least two days a term learning in the College's bushland reserve, measuring trees, writing poetry and tracking the birds that give the ridge its name. Every Junior School class visits the library each week. Learning Junior School Senior School Co-curricular Wellbeing
/learning/senior-school/: Senior School Home Learning Senior School Years 7 to 12: depth, choice and preparation for life after school. In Years 7 and 8 students study a broad core of subjects and try electives across the arts, technology and languages. From Year 9 they choose electives, and in Years 11 and 12 they follow a Higher School Certificate pattern built around their strengths and goals. Subjects offered in Years 11 and 12 Area Subjects English English Advanced, English Standard, Extension 1 and 2 Mathematics Standard, Advanced, Extension 1 and 2 Science Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Earth and Environmental Science HASS Modern History, Ancient History, Geography, Economics, Legal Studies, Business Studies Arts Music 1 and 2, Visual Arts, Drama Languages French Continuers, Japanese Continuers Other PDHPE, Design and Technology, Software Engineering Careers and pathways Our careers adviser meets every student in Years 10, 11 and 12. Students take part in work experience in Year 10 and university visits in Year 11. Learning Junior School Senior School Co-curricular Wellbeing
/learning/co-curricular/: Co-curricular Home Learning Co-curricular More than forty clubs, teams and ensembles, before school, at lunchtime and after school. Sport Students can play in eleven sports, including football, netball, basketball, hockey, cricket, tennis, rowing and cross country. Every student also competes for one of the four houses in the swimming, athletics and cross-country carnivals. Music Around a third of our students learn an instrument. Ensembles include the concert band, string ensemble, jazz band, Junior School choir, Senior choir and a chamber choir. The Performing Arts Centre seats 480. Debating and public speaking Teams from Year 5 to Year 12 compete in regional debating competitions, and our senior students take part in mock trial and model United Nations. Robotics and coding The robotics club meets twice a week in the Science Centre. Teams design, build and program robots for state and regional challenges. Learning Junior School Senior School Co-curricular Wellbeing
/learning/wellbeing/: Wellbeing Home Learning Wellbeing Students learn best when they feel safe, known and supported. Every student belongs to a pastoral care group that meets each morning with the same teacher for several years. Heads of Year, the College counsellor and our chaplaincy team work together to support students and families. Our program Peer support : Year 11 leaders mentor every new Year 7 student. Positive education lessons each fortnight, from Kindergarten to Year 10. Digital wellbeing workshops for students and parents. Counselling , available to any student, confidentially. The small things matter most: a teacher who says hello by name, a friend who saves you a seat. — Year 8 student Learning Junior School Senior School Co-curricular Wellbeing
